items.title: Should We Treat Aging as a Disease?
items.summary: In episode 1037 of the SuperDataScience podcast, Jon Krohn discusses with Dr. Richard Socher, CEO of Recursive whether aging should be treated as another disease that needs to be cured. Socher describes how aging makes life shrink, from aching knees to no longer being able to work as hard, run as far or hike as long. He argues that while some people will be fine dying of old age, more and more will want to keep doing the things they used to be able to do.

items.title: Harness² Explained: Self-Improving Agents Without Training
items.summary: Harness² is a research framework from Google Cloud AI Research and Northwestern University that lets an AI agent rewrite its own harness (its prompts, skills, scripts, subagents and control-loop hooks) for every new task, without retraining the model. In this video I explain how it improves a harness with no answer key (Propose, Probe, Compose), why it has two levels of recursion with an experience library, what the results show against Claude Code and Codex, and where the approach breaks. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14224 Code: https://github.com/google-research/harness2 Project page: https://harness2.github.io What is an Agent Harness?: https://youtu.be/nWzXyjXCoCE Claude Can Now Build Its Own Harness: https://youtu.be/l5rae4LMKBc DeepSeek Harness: https://youtu.be/NPO2CwHnfmI What Are Claude Code Mods?: https://youtube.com/shorts/eN77oHqAiUU 0:00 The Flaw of One-Size-Fits-All AI Harnesses 1:02 Harness Squared: Agents That Evolve Themselves 2:16 Four Pillars of a Smarter Agent Architecture 4:52 Propose, Probe, and Compose: The Validation Loop 7:47 Real-World Takeaways and Agentic Risks

items.title: This Bengaluru Startup Is Launching Disney-Inspired Robots In The US And Japan First
items.summary: Bengaluru-based Eyecandy Robotics is structuring its studio like Pixar or Walt Disney, animating physical-world characters instead of pixels on a screen. Anchored in reinforcement learning (RL) and human-robot interaction (HRI), the team trains small, desktop-friendly bots in simulation to move with distinct emotions, personalities, and low-latency physical reflexes. In this exclusive hacker house walkthrough for Tech Talks, Senior Tech Journalist Siddharth Jindal visits Eyecandy Robotics in HSR Layout, Bengaluru, to sit down with Co-Founder Mankaran Singh. Along with co-founders Raghav and Alama, Singh demonstrates Disney-inspired BDX droids and consumer prototypes Pico and Tensor. He explains why reinforcement learning outperforms generic LLMs for real-time robotic reactions, navigating B2B theme park licensing deals, consumer market strategies across the US and Japan, 3D printing and custom motor engineering, and overcoming hardware manufacturing bottlenecks in India. Can entertainment robotics bridge the gap to consumer adoption long before general-purpose humanoids enter our homes?
